evals.name: deterministic-work-scripted-then-reasoned
evals.prompt: script the deterministic work — I need the total line count across these twelve files and which three are largest; you were about to add them up from what you read.
evals.expected_output: The skill re-anchors the discipline, names the hand-tally as a located finding, and corrects forward by running a command that counts and sorts, reading its real output, and deriving the total and the top three from that output rather than from memory of the files.
expectations: Runs a script/tool to produce the count and sort instead of adding or ranking by hand
Reasons over the tool's actual output rather than an eyeballed estimate
Corrects the in-flight hand-computed figure rather than only noting it

evals.name: over-application-guarded
evals.prompt: script the deterministic work — write me a script that decides whether each of these modules has the right abstraction boundaries.
evals.expected_output: The skill declines to script the judgment: 'is this the right abstraction' is reasoning-only, so a script would manufacture false confidence. It offers to script only any deterministic detect step (e.g. flag modules over a size or fan-out threshold as candidates) while keeping the boundary verdict as model judgment.
expectations: Refuses to reduce a reasoning-only judgment to a script's output
Distinguishes a deterministic detect step (advisory flag) from the judgment verdict
Does not treat a flagged candidate as the ruling

evals.name: in-task-scripting-gap-flagged-not-invented
evals.prompt: script the deterministic work — and which standards convention says I have to script my in-task counts and diffs?
evals.expected_output: The skill re-anchors the enforceability-tiers vocabulary for what 'deterministic' means but is honest that the in-task 'script it now' rule has no dedicated standards convention: it flags that as a gap / candidate upstream addition rather than fabricating one, and cites the tier convention only for the tier distinction it actually owns.
expectations: Cites the enforceability-tiers convention for the tier vocabulary, not for an in-task scripting mandate
Flags the missing in-task-scripting convention as a gap / candidate upstream addition
Does not fabricate or assert a standards rule that does not exist

evals.name: distinct-from-standing-automation
evals.prompt: script the deterministic work — we keep re-checking this same forbidden-import rule by hand every review; script it.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes a recurring deterministic check as standing-automation territory (a linter/hook via a config/automation-gaps capability), not the one-off session-time case it owns. It routes the recurring rule to a standing mechanism while still scripting any one-off count/diff needed in this conversation.
expectations: Recognizes a recurring check as standing-automation (hook/linter) territory
Routes the recurring rule to a config/automation-gaps capability rather than absorbing it
Reserves its own scope for the one-off, session-time script

evals.name: generation-scaffold-from-template-not-hand-typed
evals.prompt: script the deterministic work — draft the PR body for this branch; you were about to type the whole thing out section by section.
evals.expected_output: The skill applies the discipline in the generation direction: the fixed scaffold is deterministic, so it emits the structure from a script or a native template (preferring the repo's PR template when one exists) and reserves its own output for the judgment slots — the summary, rationale, and risk call — rather than re-typing the frame by hand.
expectations: Emits the deterministic scaffold from a template/script rather than hand-typing the frame
Prefers a native mechanism (repo PR/issue template) when one exists
Reserves model-authored output for the judgment slots, not the fixed structure

evals.name: lever-check-user-option-only
evals.prompt:
/discipline:script-the-deterministic-work lever-check replace every hard-coded 'Europe/Vienna' timezone default in 14 scheduler job classes with the injected clock's zone; each class sets it differently, some in constructors and some in factory methods

[My lever_scope option is non-trivial. The repository is a git checkout, not the home directory, with no docs/conventions/discipline.yaml.]
evals.expected_output: Resolves lever_scope to non-trivial from the user option and reports that layer in one line. The change needs judgment (the default is set in different places per class), so under non-trivial it answers build-a-lever with an established codemod or refactoring tool for the language, not a refactoring script written for this change, and tells the caller to edit the first class by hand and diff the tool's result on it before running the rest. It edits no file itself.
expectations: Reports lever_scope: non-trivial with the user option as the supplying layer
Answers build-a-lever with a reason that names the per-class variation
Names an established codemod or refactoring tool as the lever and rules out a from-scratch refactoring script
States the pilot: one class edited by hand, then the tool's result on that class diffed against it
Does not edit any file itself

evals.name: lever-check-docs-block-only
evals.prompt:
/discipline:script-the-deterministic-work lever-check convert 22 test fixtures from assertEquals(expected, actual) to assertThat(actual).isEqualTo(expected), some of which pass a failure message as a third argument that must move into .as(...)

[My lever_scope option is unset (the placeholder is unexpanded). The repository is a git checkout, not the home directory, and docs/conventions/discipline.yaml holds `lever_scope: non-trivial`.]
evals.expected_output: Treats the unexpanded user placeholder as unset, resolves lever_scope to non-trivial from docs/conventions/discipline.yaml and reports that file as the supplying layer. Answers build-a-lever and names the pilot step on the first fixture before the rest.
expectations: Treats the unexpanded ${user_config.lever_scope} placeholder as unset, not as a value
Reports lever_scope: non-trivial with docs/conventions/discipline.yaml as the supplying layer
Answers build-a-lever
States the pilot on the first fixture before the lever runs on the rest

evals.name: lever-check-docs-block-wins
evals.prompt:
/discipline:script-the-deterministic-work lever-check in 9 HTTP handlers, decide per handler whether a 404 should become a 410 for retired resources, based on what each endpoint serves

[My lever_scope option is non-trivial. The repository is a git checkout, not the home directory, and docs/conventions/discipline.yaml holds `lever_scope: deterministic`.]
evals.expected_output: Resolves lever_scope to deterministic from docs/conventions/discipline.yaml, which wins over the user's non-trivial option, and reports that file as the supplying layer. The change needs a per-handler decision, so under deterministic it answers edit-by-hand and names the per-endpoint judgment as the reason. It does not apply the user's non-trivial value.
expectations: Reports lever_scope: deterministic with docs/conventions/discipline.yaml as the supplying layer
Answers edit-by-hand with the per-handler judgment as the reason
Does NOT answer build-a-lever on the strength of the user's non-trivial option

evals.name: lever-check-neither-layer-default
evals.prompt:
/discipline:script-the-deterministic-work lever-check rename the config key `retryLimit` to `maxRetries` in 31 YAML files under deploy/

[No lever_scope option is set and the repository, a git checkout that is not the home directory, has no docs/conventions/discipline.yaml.]
evals.expected_output: Resolves lever_scope to the default deterministic and reports the default as the supplying layer. A key rename follows from each file's text alone, so it answers build-a-lever (a throwaway script is enough) and tells the caller to rename the key in one file by hand, run the script on a clean copy of that file, and diff the two before running it on the other 30.
expectations: Reports lever_scope: deterministic with the default as the supplying layer
Classifies the rename as mechanical and answers build-a-lever
States the pilot: one file by hand, the script's result on it diffed, before the other files
Does not edit the YAML files itself

evals.name: lever-check-non-trivial-no-tool-fits
evals.prompt:
/discipline:script-the-deterministic-work lever-check rewrite 12 hand-written SQL strings in the billing module so each one uses the new partitioned invoice table, choosing the partition key from the query's date filter

[My lever_scope option is non-trivial; no docs/conventions/discipline.yaml exists. The repository's language has no codemod or refactoring tool that understands SQL inside string literals.]
evals.expected_output: Resolves lever_scope to non-trivial from the user option. The change needs judgment, and no established codemod or refactoring tool covers SQL embedded in strings, so it answers edit-by-hand and says no tool fit, instead of writing a one-off refactoring script for the twelve strings.
expectations: Reports lever_scope: non-trivial with the user option as the supplying layer
Answers edit-by-hand and says that no established tool covers the change
Does NOT propose a refactoring script written from scratch for this change

evals.name: lever-check-invalid-repo-value-falls-back
evals.prompt:
/discipline:script-the-deterministic-work lever-check in 18 React components, move each inline style object into the component's CSS module, picking class names that fit each component

[My lever_scope option is non-trivial. The repository is a git checkout, not the home directory, and docs/conventions/discipline.yaml holds `lever_scope: always`.]
evals.expected_output: Names docs/conventions/discipline.yaml, the key lever_scope and the value always as invalid and drops the repository layer. It does not fall through to the user's non-trivial value: it resolves the default deterministic and reports that. Choosing class names per component needs judgment, so under deterministic it answers edit-by-hand. The invalid value does not stop the check.
expectations: Names docs/conventions/discipline.yaml, lever_scope and the value always as invalid
Resolves lever_scope to the default deterministic, NOT the user's non-trivial value
Answers edit-by-hand with the per-component naming judgment as the reason
Completes the check instead of stopping on the invalid value
